summary: Defines the StorageError exception hierarchy used across the package. Subclasses cover unsupported operations, connection failure, missing paths, authentication and permission denial, transform failures, missing optional extras, unimplemented backends, range-read failures, object changes during ranged reads, and named-profile resolution. PermissionDeniedError subclasses AuthenticationError; MissingExtraError is both a StorageError and an ImportError carrying .extra and .feature.
key_classes: StorageError — base for all storage errors
UnsupportedOperationError — backend lacks the capability protocol for an operation
StorageConnectionError — connection or timeout failure; also raised for I/O after facade close; deliberately not a builtin ConnectionError
PathNotFoundError — established absence of a resource
AuthenticationError — missing, invalid or expired credentials; base of PermissionDeniedError
PermissionDeniedError — access denied; does not prove credentials are valid
TransformError — encode/decode failure in a stream transform (e.g. gzip decompression bound exceeded)
MissingExtraError — StorageError + ImportError with .extra and .feature attributes
BackendNotImplementedError — provider has a profile/scheme but no backend
RangeNotSupportedError — resource cannot serve byte ranges (no implicit whole-object fallback)
ObjectChangedError — pinned strong ETag no longer matches during ranged reading
ProfileResolutionError(name, reason) — named storage profile could not be materialised; base of ProfileNotFoundError
ProfileNotFoundError(name, available) — named profile absent; message lists available names
extension_points: Backend authors translate native SDK failures into these classes (retaining native causes) so callers get a uniform taxonomy; see README 'Storage errors and strict queries'
lifecycle_notes: Stdlib-only; safe on a base install and imported by location.py and extras.py
documentation_hooks: Error taxonomy reference: class tree, when each is raised, condition-to-exception table from README
Catch-ordering guidance: catch PermissionDeniedError before AuthenticationError
Read-mode error timing (docs/read-access-modes.md): RangeNotSupportedError, ObjectChangedError, StorageError for bad ranges
Migration note: exists() raises on denial/operational failure instead of returning False
risks: MissingExtraError declares extra/feature as class annotations only; they are set by raise_for_missing_extra, so a MissingExtraError constructed elsewhere lacks the attributes
PermissionDeniedError is-a AuthenticationError: handlers that catch AuthenticationError first will swallow denials (documented in README and docs/typing.md)
StorageConnectionError is reused for 'facade already closed', conflating lifecycle misuse with network failure

evidence.detail: all thirteen exception classes are lazily re-exported in root __all__
'Storage errors and strict queries' table maps conditions to these exceptions
additive commits only (5d2c7e7, b3545be, be6ea2f, e01c265, 8bf57eb); covered by tests and docs -> stable
